substory_punchline: Within-ecotype, within-substudy meta-analysis surfaces six actionable pathobionts that replicate at 88% on a held-out cohort

content.punchline: Within-ecotype, within-substudy meta-analysis surfaces six actionable pathobionts that replicate at 88% on a held-out cohort

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Bridge from S1: now that ecotypes exist and patients are distributed non-randomly across them, stratification makes something possible that was structurally impossible in the pooled cohort — a confound-free CD-vs-nonIBD contrast. The key setup: cMD's study nesting means zero sub-studies contain both HC and CD samples, so a pooled CD-vs-HC LME is unidentifiable. Within IBD sub-studies, CD-vs-nonIBD IS identifiable within each study. Stratify by ecotype before meta-analysis and you get Tier-A lists that are free of both leakage and study confounding. E1 Tier-A replicates at 88.2% on HMP2; E3 Tier-A is provisional. Six targets cleared a multi-criteria score threshold of 2.5.

content.title: Methods: within-ecotype × within-substudy meta-analysis eliminates two structural confounds, then five-criterion scoring narrows to actionable targets
bullets: Pooled CD-vs-HC is unidentifiable in cMD: zero sub-studies have both CD and HC; LME random effect perfectly predicts diagnosis (statsmodels.mixedlm fails silently)

Confound-free design: CD-vs-nonIBD within each IBD sub-study (HallAB_2017, LiJ_2014, IjazUZ_2017, NielsenHB_2014); CLR-Δ computed on same-study samples, then inverse-variance weighted meta across sub-studies
Stratify by ecotype before meta-analysis: samples partitioned by ecotype (clustering axis); CLR-Δ computed within partition (DA axis) — no feature-leakage self-reference
Three (sub-study × ecotype × diagnosis) cells pass ≥10 CD + ≥10 nonIBD: E1 × HallAB_2017 + E1 × NielsenHB_2014 (meta-viable); E3 × HallAB_2017 only (single-study, provisional)
NB04h HMP2 external replication: 1,627 samples projected onto K=4 LDA; per-species CD-vs-nonIBD CLR-Δ in HMP2-projected E1 (593 CD / 337 nonIBD) cross-referenced against 51-candidate E1 Tier-A

NB05 multi-criterion scoring: A3 literature + cohort CD-association (0–5), A4 protective-analog exclusion (0/1), A5 virulence-mechanism support (0–2), A6 BGC inflammatory mediator (0/0.5/1); total_score ≥ 2.5 threshold applied to 71 rigor-controlled candidates

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Walk through each bullet in order. The key methodological insight is that the pooled cohort design CANNOT answer the question — not a matter of statistical power, a structural identifiability failure. The within-substudy CD-vs-nonIBD contrast is the only identifiable contrast in cMD. The ecotype stratification is then a second layer: partition samples by ecotype FIRST (this uses the clustering axis), then compute CLR-Δ across sub-studies WITHIN each partition (this uses the DA axis). These two axes are disjoint — no feature appears in both, so no selection-on-outcome leakage. Emphasize: E1 is meta-viable (two sub-studies); E3 is single-study-only (HallAB_2017 only), flagged provisional from the start. NB05 scoring applies five criteria to the 71-candidate union set. Source: REPORT.md §5 (NB04e) + §5f (NB04h) + §7 (NB05).

content.title: Confound-free meta-analysis yields six actionable E1 pathobionts — E1 robust, E3 provisional pending replication
bullets: E1 Tier-A: 51 candidates, meta-viable across HallAB_2017 + NielsenHB_2014 (82 CD / 280 nonIBD), all 100% sign-concordant; top candidates include M. gnavus (CLR-Δ +4.85), S. salivarius (+3.26), E. innocuum (+2.65)
NB05 scoring of 71 rigor-controlled candidates at total_score ≥ 2.5: 6 actionable targets — H. hathewayi (4.0), M. gnavus (3.8), E. coli (3.6), E. lenta (3.3), F. plautii (3.3), E. bolteae (2.8)

E3 Tier-A is preliminary evidence: 40 candidates from HallAB_2017 only (22 CD / 31 nonIBD); HMP2 has only 10 E3 subjects and cannot provide a second-study meta; 31% of UC Davis patients are E3 and inherit this provisional status

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This slide covers A5 (✓ direct). The 88.2% figure is verbatim from REPORT §5f: '45/51 (88.2%) are sign-concordant (both CD↑).' The HMP2 cohort (HMP_2019_ibdmdb) was NOT in the cMD training set — it was pulled live via curatedMetagenomicData v3.18 and held out for this exact replication test. The 593 CD / 337 nonIBD E1 slice is from REPORT §5f. Top replicators include M. gnavus (HMP2 +1.08, FDR 3e-13), E. bolteae (+1.27, FDR 2e-18), H. symbiosa (+1.18, FDR 6e-22). Only 2 of the top 20 fail (S. thermophilus possibly due to dairy exposure difference; B. stercoris n.s.). Important nuance: the ecotype FRAMEWORK has LOSO ARI 0.113 (cross-study variable), but the operational Tier-A replicates at 88.2% — framework stability and target-list replication are distinct properties (Novel Contribution #11). This is the clearest rebuttal to 'reproducible ecotypes overstates evidence.'

evidence_anchors.ref: REPORT.md §5f (NB04h: 45/51 = 88.2% sign-concordant; HMP2 593 CD / 337 nonIBD in E1)

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This slide covers A7 (✓ direct). The key finding from REPORT §5h (NB06 H2d): 'In every subnet, a single module contains 4-5 of the 6 actionable Tier-A candidates' (module sizes 57–84 nodes). The verbatim REPORT numbers are: E1_all module 1 size 84 with E. lenta, E. bolteae, F. plautii, H. hathewayi, M. gnavus; E3_CD module 1 size 57 with E. lenta, E. coli, H. hathewayi, M. gnavus. Biological implication (REPORT §5h): 'ecological coupling suggests a cocktail hitting 3+ of {M. gnavus, E. lenta, E. bolteae, H. hathewayi, E. coli} will have compounding effects.' The ecotype-specific membership is mechanistically load-bearing for Substory 3's per-patient cocktail design: F. plautii is E1-specific, E. coli is E3-specific, which constrains which targets go into each patient's cocktail. Note for speaker: E1_CD module 0 size is approximate — REPORT §5h verbatim gives E1_all module 1 (84) and E3_CD module 1 (57); the E1_CD number comes from NB06 notebook output table.
